He played four seasons of [[college basketball]] for the [[Mississippi State Bulldogs men's basketball|Mississippi State Bulldogs]]. Weatherspoon was selected 49th overall by the [[San Antonio Spurs]] in the [[2019 NBA Draft|2019 NBA draft]]. After two seasons with the team, he joined the [[Golden State Warriors]] in 2021. During his first season with the Warriors, he won an [[List of NBA champions|NBA championship]]. ==Early life== Born in [[Canton, Mississippi]], Weatherspoon is the son of Sharon and Tommie Weatherspoon and has two younger brothers, Nick and Brandon, who are also basketball players. He began playing basketball in middle school. He starred at [[Velma Jackson High School]], where he was coached by Anthony Carlyle. Velma Jackson won three straight state titles in 2012, 2013 and 2014.{{cite news|last1=Greever|first1=Tyler|title=A Basketball Brotherhood: The Three Weatherspoons|url=https://www.wjtv.com/sports/a-basketball-brotherhood-the-three-weatherspoons/|access-date=July 3, 2018|work=WJTV|date=December 27, 2015|archive-date=July 10, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190710022717/https://www.wjtv.com/sports/a-basketball-brotherhood-the-three-weatherspoons/|url-status=dead}} Towards the end of his high school career, he was considered a three-star recruit, ranked no. 116 in his class by Rivals.com and later committed to [[Mississippi State Bulldogs men's basketball|Mississippi State]] under [[Ben Howland]]. ==College career== Weatherspoon was named to the SEC All-Freshman Team.{{cite press release|url=http://www.secsports.com/article/14925031/2016-sec-men-basketball-awards-announced|title=2016 SEC Men's Basketball Awards Announced|publisher=[[Southeastern Conference]]|date=March 8, 2016|access-date=July 3, 2018}} He averaged 12.0 points and 4.7 rebounds per game playing alongside [[Malik Newman]].{{cite news|last1=Parrish|first1=Gary|title=Recruiting Roundup: Ben Howland building another solid class at Mississippi State|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/recruiting-roundup-ben-howland-building-another-solid-class-at-mississippi-state/|access-date=July 3, 2018|work=[[CBS Sports]]|date=September 12, 2016}} He injured his wrist against [[Boise State Broncos men's basketball|Boise State]] on November 21, 2016, and was initially ruled out for the season.{{cite news|last1=Norlander|first1=Matt|title=Mississippi State loses Quinndary Weatherspoon for season: 3 things to know|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/mississippi-state-loses-quinndary-weatherspoon-for-season-3-things-to-know/|access-date=July 3, 2018|work=[[CBS Sports]]|date=November 22, 2016}} After missing several games, Weatherspoon came back.{{cite news|last1=Jones|first1=Paul|title=MSU's Quinndary Weatherspoon Updates Offseason Rehab Progress|url=https://247sports.com/article/msus-quinndary-weatherspoon-updates-offseason-rehab-progress-105545343/|access-date=July 3, 2018|work=247sports|date=July 27, 2017}} As a sophomore, Weatherspoon averaged 16.5 points and 5.1 rebounds per game.{{cite news|last1=Cloninger|first1=David|title=Previewing SEC basketball: Mississippi State|url=https://www.postandcourier.com/sports/previewing-sec-basketball-mississippi-state/article_2ef48556-c16f-11e7-b51a-a354a7118bf4.html |access-date=July 3, 2018 |work=[[The Post and Courier]]|date=November 4, 2017}} Weatherspoon was named to the Second Team All-SEC as a sophomore.{{cite press release|url=http://www.secsports.com/article/18844347/2017-sec-men-basketball-awards-announced|title=2017 SEC Men's Basketball Awards Announced|publisher=[[Southeastern Conference]]|date=March 7, 2017|access-date=July 3, 2018}} As a junior, Weatherspoon averaged 14.4 points, 6.0 rebounds and 3.3 assists per game and started every game. He earned the [[Howell Trophy]] as the best player in Mississippi.{{cite news|title=Mississippi State's Quinndary Weatherspoon declares for NBA Draft|url=https://www.clarionledger.com/story/sports/college/mississippi-state/2018/04/06/mississippi-states-quinndary-weatherspoon-declares-nba-draft/495220002/|access-date=July 3, 2018|work=[[Clarion Ledger]]|date=April 6, 2018}} Weatherspoon was named second-team All-SEC.{{cite press release|url=http://www.secsports.com/article/22657404/2018-sec-men-basketball-awards-announced|title=2018 SEC Men's Basketball Awards announced|publisher=[[Southeastern Conference]]|date=March 6, 2018|access-date=July 3, 2018}} On April 6, 2018, Weatherspoon joined his brother Nick Weatherspoon and Lamar Peters among Mississippi State players to declare for the [[2018 NBA draft]].{{cite news|last=Coleman|first=Joel|title=State's Quinndary Weatherspoon latest to declare for NBA Draft|url=https://www.starkvilledailynews.com/content/states-quinndary-weatherspoon-latest-declare-nba-draft|access-date=July 3, 2018|work=[[Starkville Daily News]]|date=April 6, 2018|archive-date=April 9, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180409164556/http://starkvilledailynews.com/content/states-quinndary-weatherspoon-latest-declare-nba-draft|url-status=dead}} He later opted to withdraw from the draft and return to Mississippi State.{{cite news|last1=Reiss|first1=Aaron|title=SEC basketball got a boost after these players withdrew from the NBA Draft|url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/sec/article212261829.html|access-date=July 3, 2018|work=[[Kansas City Star]]|date=May 31, 2018}} In his senior season, Weatherspoon was named first-team All-SEC. He became the program's third player to score 2,000 career points on March 22, 2019, in an upset loss to [[Liberty Flames basketball|Liberty]] on the [[2019 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2019 NCAA tournament]].{{cite news|last1=Eble|first1=Tom|title=Liberty upsets Mississippi State in round one|url=https://www.wcbi.com/liberty-upsets-mississippi-state-round-one/|access-date=March 23, 2019|work=wcbi.com|date=March 22, 2019}} ==Professional career== ===San Antonio Spurs (2019–2021)=== On 21, 2019}} Weatherspoon was later listed in the roster of Spurs for the [[2019 NBA Summer League]] hosted at [[Vivint Arena]].{{cite web|title=SPURS ANNOUNCE 2019 SALT LAKE CITY SUMMER LEAGUE ROSTER|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/spurs-announce-2019-salt-lake-city-summer-league-roster|website=NBA.com|date=June 26, 2019|access-date=June 26, 2019}} On July 8, 2019, Weatherspoon signed a [[two-way contract]] with the Spurs.{{cite web|title=SPURS SIGN QUINNDARY WEATHERSPOON TO TWO-WAY CONTRACT|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-sign-quinndary-weatherspoon-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=July 8, 2019|access-date=July 8, 2019}} He had a career-high 30 points for the [[Austin Spurs]] in a 126–123 overtime win over the [[Greensboro Swarm]] on January 4, 2020.{{cite news|first=Jeff|last=Garcia|title=Spurs' Weatherspoon scores a career-high against Swarm in Austin February 8, 2020, Weatherspoon had his debut in the NBA, coming off from bench in a 102–122 loss to the [[Sacramento Kings]].{{cite web |date=February 8, 2020 |title=Hield, Kings heat up to keep Spurs reeling, 122–102 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401161427 |access-date=February 9, 2020 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press}} On November 24, 2020, the Spurs announced that they had
